common_name: Park Side Live Oak (Branch-Structure-Selected Live Oak for Streets and Parking Lots)

planting.note: Plant container trees in fall or early spring in well-drained to moist, deep soil in full sun; Park Side is a live oak selection bred for wide branch attachment angles and dense secondary branching, giving it superior structure for boulevard and parking-lot plantings.

directions: Plant in well-drained to moist, deep soil in full sun, giving it ample room to reach its ultimate 60-foot height and spread. Park Side was selected and developed specifically to meet commercial grading standards for branch structure, with secondary branches attaching at unusually wide angles and abundant twiggy growth off the larger limbs, producing a denser, more structurally sound canopy earlier than seedling-grown or many other clonal live oaks. This makes it a strong choice for boulevards, parking-lot islands, and windbreak plantings where branch failure and included bark are persistent problems with wide-spreading street trees. Once established it shares the species' drought and flood tolerance, wind resistance, and tolerance of varied soil pH; water deeply during the first two to three years and prune only to remove crossing or weakly attached limbs.
sources: Fish Branch Tree Farm cultivar description
Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services Grades and Standards for Nursery Plants

common_name: Boardwalk Live Oak (Formal Pyramidal Live Oak with Reduced Acorn Drop)

planting.note: Plant container trees in fall or early spring in well-drained to moist, deep soil in full sun; Boardwalk is a live oak selection with a dominant central leader and a dense, formally pyramidal canopy that holds its shape well into maturity.

directions: Plant in well-drained to moist, deep soil in full sun; Boardwalk grows fast as a juvenile and responds especially well to structural pruning during its first years in the landscape. It keeps a strongly dominant central leader with branches attaching at wide angles, and short, twiggy lateral growth gives the canopy a dense, somewhat formal pyramidal outline that is unusual among live oak selections. Growers also report that it produces noticeably fewer acorns than straight-species live oak or other clonal cultivars, a useful trait near sidewalks, patios, and parking areas. Water deeply during establishment; once rooted in it shares the species' wind resistance, tolerance of varied soils and moisture, and long-lived, evergreen character.
sources: Fish Branch Tree Farm cultivar description
Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services Grades and Standards for Nursery Plants

common_name: Sky Climber Live Oak (Upright Pyramidal Live Oak Selection)

planting.note: Plant container trees in fall or early spring in well-drained to moist, deep soil in full sun; Sky Climber is a live oak selection with consistent upright growth and a dense pyramidal crown, useful where a more formal, uniform street-tree silhouette is wanted.

directions: Plant in well-drained to moist, deep soil in full sun to partial shade. Sky Climber was selected for its consistently upright growth habit and dense, pyramidal crown of glossy dark green leaves, giving it a more uniform silhouette than the broad, irregularly spreading form typical of straight-species live oak, which makes it useful as a street tree or in mass plantings where a tidier profile is wanted. It flowers inconspicuously in spring and sets the usual small acorns in fall, which support birds and other wildlife. Established trees tolerate salt spray, wind, and periodic drought; water deeply during the first few years and prune minimally to preserve the natural upright form.
sources: Devil Mountain Wholesale Nursery cultivar description
